name: Uruguay
headline_status: Uruguay was the first country to fully legalise recreational cannabis; registered adult citizens and residents can grow it, join clubs or buy it in pharmacies.
summary: Law 19.172, signed on 23 December 2013, created a state-regulated cannabis market overseen by the IRCCA. Registered adults 18+ can choose one of three routes: growing up to six plants at home, joining a cannabis club, or buying up to 40 g a month in licensed pharmacies, which began selling in 2017. Visitors are currently excluded, but in early 2026 the regulator said it was studying ways to let non-residents buy legally.

adult_use_since.value: Law 19.172 signed 23 December 2013; pharmacy sales began in 2017.

possession_limit.value: Registered pharmacy buyers may purchase up to 40 g per month.

home_grow.value: Up to six plants per household, with an annual harvest of no more than 480 g; growers must register.

retail_sales.value: Sold in licensed pharmacies to registered users, verified by fingerprint at purchase; registered cannabis clubs of 15 to 45 members may grow up to 99 plants a year.

regulator.value: Institute for the Regulation and Control of Cannabis (IRCCA), created in August 2014.

tourists.value: Non-residents cannot register and so cannot legally buy, and taking cannabis across borders is banned. In 2026 the IRCCA said it was studying allowing tourists, students and temporary workers to buy under controlled conditions.

timeline.event: President Mujica signs Law 19.172 legalising and regulating cannabis
Pharmacy sales to registered users begin
IRCCA says it is evaluating legal sales to non-resident foreigners

pending.item: Regulatory change to let non-resident foreigners, including tourists, buy legal cannabis.
pending.status: Under evaluation by the IRCCA since early 2026; nothing approved.

faq.a: Yes. Registered adults can grow up to six plants, join a cannabis club or buy up to 40 g a month at licensed pharmacies.

faq.q: Can tourists buy weed in Uruguay?
faq.a: Not currently. Only registered citizens and residents can buy, though the regulator is studying opening sales to visitors.

faq.q: How much weed can you buy in Uruguay?
faq.a: Registered pharmacy customers can buy up to 40 g per month.
